per_item.SEC_F1: fixed as Addition 4 says: services/audit.js:158-159 reads currentAppRole (one constant statement, audit-store.js:16-21) and throws TypeError before lockChain unless app.role is 'platform'. Probe: under withTenant the writer throws and audit_log is unchanged; with no app.role and with 'worker' it throws too; a platform write follows and the whole chain verifies (sp5, sp2: verify ok). Every M2.2 caller runs in the pipeline's platform transaction: sp1 (all auth and admin routes) passes 125/125 with the chain verifying at the end.
per_item.SEC_F2: fixed: rate-limit.js:26-42 addressKey (IPv4 whole, IPv6 by its /64 as a:b:c:d::/64, 'unknown' as it is) is used for every address limit (rate-limit.js:58; the user limit keeps the session id) and for the admin delay key (auth.js:384); ip_hmac keeps the whole address. Own literal oracle over 12 forms (compressed, full, leading zeros, '::', '::1', link-local, an IPv4 tail, '::' in the middle) all match; 20k calls well under 200 ms. Probe: 11 logins from 11 addresses of one /64 → the 11th is 429; another /64 and an IPv4 address keep their own windows; the admin delay row is shared by the /64 (429) while a clean /64 signs in at once; the delay key is mac(delay, 2001:db8:9:9::/64); ip_hmac of the session is that of the whole address. An IPv6 key cannot collide with an IPv4 key or 'unknown' (they hold no ':').
per_item.SEC_F3: fixed: uat-login.js:160-186 opens the secret file once with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW (ELOOP → 'is a symbolic link'), checks isFile and the mode by fstat on that descriptor, reads from it, and closes it in finally (also on a returned refusal). The open stands after the win32 refusal, so the missing O_NOFOLLOW constant of Windows is never used. Probe sp4 18/18 (the win32 refusal before any read or fetch; the POSIX branch refuses a group/other-readable file through the new fstat). The link-swap case itself needs Linux (UL-2 of the design, CI).
per_item.SEC_F4: named as Addition 4 says: design section 7 gains the residual row (3 pool connections held through scrypt, measured after the deploy); no code change, as asked.
per_item.SEC_F5: fixed: auth.js:545-546 deleteUnusedResets(req.q, row.id) in the password-change transaction, after the current password verified. Probe: after a password change the user's unused code answers 400 reset_invalid; the admin's own password change leaves another user's code usable (scoped by user id).
